1 small onion, finely chopped: 1 tomato, grated
Preheat the oven to 190 °C; toss the potatoes with olive oil and bake for 15 minutes.
Fry the onion and mince, add the tomato paste and tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Arrange the potatoes in a baking dish and spread the mince mixture over them.
Add the hot water, cover and bake for 25 minutes.
Use little salt; the daily salt limit for children is lower than for adults.
2 leeks (white and light green parts)
Halve the leeks lengthwise, wash between the layers in plenty of water and slice into 2 cm rings.
Toss the carrot in olive oil for 2 minutes, then the leek for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and hot water and cook covered over a low heat for 25 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and leave to cool in the pot.
Offer new vegetables to children alongside a familiar food.
Oven tray of meatballs and vegetables
150 g beef mince
1 tablespoon grated onion
1 zucchini, 1 carrot and 1 potato, roughly chopped
Knead the mince, breadcrumbs, onion and cumin and shape small meatballs.
Toss the vegetables with olive oil, spread on a tray and bake for 15 minutes.
Place the meatballs among the vegetables and bake 20 more minutes until cooked through.
One-tray meals save time on busy days.
Lentil soup (family style)
Soften the onion in butter for 3 minutes.
Add the chopped carrot, potato and washed lentils and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the hot water and cook over a low heat for 30 minutes.
Blend, add the cumin and simmer for 2 more minutes.
Serve with lemon and croutons.
Eating the same meal as a family makes it easier for a child to accept new tastes.
Oat and peanut butter balls
3 tablespoons unsweetened peanut butter
4 pitted dates, finely chopped
Soak the dates in hot water for 10 minutes, drain and mash.
Mix all the ingredients; add milk if needed until the mixture holds its shape.
Shape hazelnut-sized balls.
Chill in the fridge for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Because of possible peanut allergy, give only a small amount the first time.
Keep the balls small and soft.
5 days in a sealed container in the fridge.
Chicken and vegetable wrap
1 wholemeal lavash
60 g grilled or boiled chicken, thinly sliced
1 lettuce leaf, finely shredded
1 tablespoon yogurt
Warm the lavash in a pan for 30 seconds to soften it.
Spread yogurt in the middle; add the chicken, carrot, lettuce and kashar.
Fold up the bottom and roll tightly.
Cut in half or into 3 cm slices and serve.
Suitable for a school/nursery lunchbox.
Baked vegetable kumpir (stuffed jacket potato)
1 large potato
2 tablespoons boiled sweetcorn
2 tablespoons finely chopped cucumber and carrot
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Wash the potato and prick it in a few places with a fork.
Bake for 50–60 minutes until a skewer goes in easily.
Split down the middle and mix the inside with butter and kashar using a fork.
Fill with the sweetcorn, vegetables and yogurt and serve.
Sweetcorn kernels can be a choking hazard for young children; mash them according to your child’s chewing skills.
Homemade granola bars
2 ripe bananas, mashed
4 dried apricots, finely chopped
Preheat the oven to 180 °C; line a 20×20 cm tin with baking paper.
Mix all the ingredients well.
Press the mixture evenly into the tin.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the edges are golden.
Cut into bars once completely cool.
Finely chopped dried fruit is used instead of whole nuts; don’t give whole nuts to children under 4.
Sweet potato purée
1 small sweet potato (about 100 g)
2–4 tablespoons drinking water, or breast milk/formula
Wash, peel and dice the sweet potato.
Steam for 12–15 minutes until a fork goes in easily.
Mash with a blender or fork.
Thin to a runny consistency with water or breast milk.
Its slightly sweet taste makes it easily accepted for first tastes.
24 hours in the fridge; can be frozen in an ice-cube tray for 1 month.
Zucchini purée
1 small zucchini (about 120 g)
Wash and peel the zucchini.
Dice and steam for 8–10 minutes.
Mash until smooth.
Add the olive oil.
Zucchini is watery, so no extra water is needed.
Carrot purée
1 medium carrot
2–3 tablespoons drinking water
Peel the carrot and slice into rounds.
Steam for 15 minutes.
Mash until smooth together with the cooking water.
Let cool and serve.
Carrots become naturally sweeter when cooked.
Pumpkin purée
150 g pumpkin
Peel and dice the pumpkin.
Steam for 12 minutes.
Mash.
Add the butter.
Roasting intensifies the flavour.
Broccoli and potato purée
4–5 small broccoli florets
2–4 tablespoons cooking water
Peel and dice the potato.
Boil the potato for 8 minutes, then with the broccoli for 6 more minutes.
Adjust the consistency with the cooking water.
Serve lukewarm.
Potato softens broccoli’s strong taste.
Apple purée (cooked)
3 tablespoons drinking water
Peel the apple and remove the core.
Dice and cook with the water for 8 minutes until soft.
In the first months, giving apple cooked makes it easier to digest.
Mashed banana
1–2 tablespoons breast milk or formula (optional)
Peel the banana.
Mash smoothly with a fork.
Thin with breast milk if needed.
Eat before it browns.
Very ripe banana is easier to mash.
Eat straight after making.
Peach purée
Score the peach skin and put it in boiling water for 30 seconds.
